svg.desc: candidate number: 35; slug: subject-to-&-wraparound-note-arbitrage; title: Subject-To & Wraparound Note Arbitrage; category: Creative real estate note spread; production stage: approved_master; scores: revenue potential: 24; profit margin potential: 24; team efficiency: 19; startup accessibility: 12; automation potential: 11; dimension max: revenue potential: 25; profit margin potential: 25; team efficiency: 20; startup accessibility: 15; automation potential: 15; total score: 90; tier label: Elite Small-Team Cash Machine; evidence confidence: High; uncertainty band: ±3 pts; uncertainty bounds: low: 87; high: 93; uncertainty note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.; score rationale: revenue potential: Revenue Potential: 24/25. Acquiring low-rate 2.75%–4.25% mortgages Subject-To and reselling via RMLO-underwritten 8.5%–9.9% wraparound notes generates upfront down-payment spreads and multi-year interest arbitrage without landlord repairs.; profit margin potential: Profit Margin Potential: 24/25. Acquiring low-rate 2.75%–4.25% mortgages Subject-To and reselling via RMLO-underwritten 8.5%–9.9% wraparound notes generates upfront down-payment spreads and multi-year interest arbitrage without landlord repairs.; team efficiency: Team Efficiency: 19/20. Acquiring low-rate 2.75%–4.25% mortgages Subject-To and reselling via RMLO-underwritten 8.5%–9.9% wraparound notes generates upfront down-payment spreads and multi-year interest arbitrage without landlord repairs.; automation potential: Automation Potential: 11/15. Acquiring low-rate 2.75%–4.25% mortgages Subject-To and reselling via RMLO-underwritten 8.5%–9.9% wraparound notes generates upfront down-payment spreads and multi-year interest arbitrage without landlord repairs.; economics: gross revenue range: $100,000–$850,000 USD annually; retained revenue range: $100,000–$850,000 USD annually; retained share: 1.0; net profit margin range: 28–52%; retained profit margin range: 28–52%; owner net profit potential: $28,000–$442,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment; startup capital range: $12,000–$65,000 USD; monthly opex range: $2,000–$12,000 USD; time to first deal: 2–6 months; automation coverage: 0.76; typical team size: full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; includes contractors note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.; revenue basis: Net upfront option/down-payment spreads and retained annual wraparound interest margin; excludes underlying home face value and pass-through debt service; cost basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.; estimate status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data; scenarios: conservative: annual gross revenue usd: 100000; annual retained revenue usd: 100000; net profit margin pct: 28; retained profit margin pct: 28.0; annual owner net profit usd: 28000; full time including owner: 1; contractors: 3; total people: 4; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Low-equity & pre-foreclosure debt triggers; Third-party licensed loan-servicer autopay; Escrow tax/insurance & underlying-payment audit; key risks: Underlying lender due-on-sale acceleration; Wrap buyer default & foreclosure carrying cost; Non-compliant seller-financing origination; regulatory notes: Underwrite every owner-occupant wraparound buyer through a licensed RMLO under SAFE Act / Dodd-Frank Ability-to-Repay rules and state wraparound disclosure statutes (e.g., Tex. Prop. Code §5.016).; Use a licensed third-party loan servicer so underlying mortgage, tax and insurance payments are verified transparently every month.; track ids: track_2; track_1; track labels: Grey-Zone Growth & Traffic Arbitrage; Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; plays: id: subject_to_wraparound_rmlo_note_spread; track id: track_2; name: Subject-To Low-Rate Mortgage Acquisition & RMLO-Underwritten Wraparound Note Spread Arbitrage; mechanism: Acquire property subject to existing 2.75%–4.25% mortgage debt and, where lawful, resell through an 8.5%–9.9% wraparound note originated with licensed RMLO involvement, applicable ability-to-repay review and licensed third-party servicing. Retain lawful origination economics and the net interest spread rather than operating as a landlord. RMLO involvement does not eliminate due-on-sale acceleration, seller liability, buyer default or property-related obligations.; inputs: Verified underlying loan, title, tax and insurance records with seller disclosures and counsel-reviewed due-on-sale analysis; Qualified buyer file and licensed RMLO underwriting with applicable SAFE Act, Dodd-Frank and state wraparound compliance; Legally reviewed transfer and wrap documents plus licensed third-party servicing, payment verification and default reserves; workflow: 1. Verify the underlying mortgage and title, disclose the seller's continuing debt exposure and obtain counsel-reviewed lender consent or a documented lawful acceleration-risk plan.; 2. Underwrite the buyer through a licensed RMLO where required and deliver all applicable consumer, financing and wraparound disclosures.; 3. Close only a lawful documented transfer with appropriate insurance and escrow arrangements, assigning property responsibilities explicitly rather than assuming none exist.; 4. Service the wrap through a licensed third party, verify underlying debt and tax payments monthly and follow lawful loss-mitigation procedures if payments fail.; metrics: Collected wrap interest less underlying interest, servicing fees and credit-loss provision; Buyer delinquency rate and percentage of underlying payments verified on time; Liquidity reserves relative to acceleration, foreclosure and property carrying exposure; platform risks: failure mode: The underlying lender accelerates debt after a subject-to transfer; trigger: Enforcement of a due-on-sale clause or a related servicing or insurance default; impact: Immediate payoff demand, refinancing costs, foreclosure exposure and harm to the original borrower; detection metric: Lender acceleration notices, unresolved servicing alerts and reserve shortfall against payoff exposure; fallback: Engage counsel and the servicer, pursue lender-approved assumption or refinancing and use a documented lawful sale or payoff exit if necessary; id: distressed_asset_recovery; track id: track_1; name: Distressed Asset Recovery; mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.; inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers; Unclaimed property & judgment dockets; Surplus auction manifests; workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances; Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value; Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts; metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case; Claim approval rate; Days from filing to disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold; trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules; impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle; detection metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance; fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required; id: probate_docket_inheritance_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Probate Docket & Pre-Foreclosure Notice-of-Default (NOD) Scraping; mechanism: Parse county probate petitions (Letters Testamentary / Letters of Administration) and daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) filings before national aggregators index them, matching out-of-state personal representatives and distressed owners to licensed probate brokers and cash buyers.; inputs: County probate court register of actions & Letters Testamentary filings; County recorder daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) & Notice-of-Trustee-Sale feeds; Skip-tracing & out-of-state personal-representative matching pipeline; workflow: Extract newly appointed estate personal representatives and real-property inventory from county probate dockets within 24 hours of filing; Cross-match parcel equity and mortgage balances against county assessor and recorder records; Deliver empathetic estate-liquidation checklists, property-preservation referrals, or licensed brokerage introductions; metrics: Docket-to-first-contact speed vs. national data aggregators (days); Personal-representative response & appointment rate (%); Commission or referral fee per closed probate/pre-foreclosure parcel; platform risks: failure mode: State Foreclosure Consultant Act violations or unlicensed brokerage fee-splitting; trigger: Charging upfront fees to distressed homeowners in NOD or taking unlicensed real-estate commission splits; impact: Voided contracts, treble damages under state foreclosure-protection statutes, or DRE enforcement; detection metric: 100% licensed broker co-marketing compliance and zero upfront homeowner fee charges; fallback: Monetize strictly via flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions to licensed probate agents or close transactions through a licensed brokerage of record; id: hoa_super_lien_tax_deed_redemption_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage; mechanism: Price small HOA priority liens and tax-sale interests using jurisdiction-specific priority, notice, and redemption rules; returns depend on enforceable rights, not assumed title extinguishment.; inputs: County tax-sale and HOA lien records; Title report and statutory redemption calendar; Local counsel priority and notice opinion; workflow: 1. Screen small-balance liens against property value, senior debt, and sale eligibility; 2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions; 3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline; 4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire; metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs; Capital days outstanding; Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate; platform risks: failure mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien; trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority; impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation; detection metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition; fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests; id: public_filing_trigger_mail_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: New-LLC & Recorded-Deed Trigger-Mail Arbitrage; mechanism: Ingest daily Secretary of State new-LLC filings and County Recorder new-deed/mortgage recordings to trigger programmatic direct mail via API—replacing illegal government-lookalike poster/deed invoices (which violate 39 U.S.C. § 3001 and state deed-solicitation laws) with high-LTV recurring workplace compliance subscriptions, property-tax appeal contingency offers, and exclusive new-mover/B2B lead monetization.; inputs: Daily Secretary of State new-entity (LLC/Corp) bulk feeds; County Recorder grant/warranty deed & mortgage recording dockets; Programmatic print-and-mail API (Lob / PostGrid) + QR intake bridge; workflow: Pull daily new-LLC formations (filtering for employer/commercial NAICS or multi-member filings) and newly recorded residential deeds with purchase price and loan metadata; Dispatch transparent, non-governmental trigger mailers within 24–48 hours of filing with personalized QR codes pre-populating entity or parcel data; Monetize new LLCs via recurring annual labor-poster/registered-agent compliance memberships and B2B partner referrals; monetize new deeds via contingency property-tax appeal filings or high-ticket homeowner lead sales; metrics: Filing-to-mailbox latency (hours); QR scan & intake conversion % per 1,000 mailers; Annualized LTV / net revenue per mailed piece; platform risks: failure mode: USPS 39 U.S.C. § 3001(h)-(i) mail-stop order, State AG UDAP enforcement, or payment-processor freeze; trigger: Styling mailers as fake government penalty notices, invoices, or charging $89-$195 solely for a $3 public deed copy without statutory disclaimers; impact: Civil restitution penalties, merchant account termination, and 30%+ chargeback rates; detection metric: Refund/chargeback ratio >1% and customer support inquiries mistaking the mailer for a government agency; fallback: Use unambiguous private commercial branding, never mimic government seals or citation numbers, and sell genuine value-add subscriptions (annual compliance updates, tax-assessment appeals, or B2B services); id: municipal_code_violation_trigger_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Municipal Code-Violation, Mechanic's Lien & Permit-Failure Lead Arbitrage; mechanism: Poll municipal building department portals and county recorder dockets daily for failed structural/fire inspections, expired permits, code citations, and newly filed mechanic's liens, routing exclusive real-time leads to remediation contractors and construction attorneys.; inputs: Municipal Accela/EnerGov building & code-enforcement portals; County recorder mechanic's lien & lis pendens dockets; Real-time Pay-Per-Call & exclusive CPL routing switch; workflow: Scrape and normalize daily municipal code citations, failed permit inspections, and recorded mechanic's liens across target metro counties; Enrich parcel owner contact records and classify urgency by abatement deadline or fine accrual rate; Route verified property owners via direct mail/outbound alerts into exclusive Pay-Per-Call or CPL agreements with licensed remediation contractors; metrics: Citation-to-outreach latency (hours); Qualified homeowner/commercial call conversion %; Revenue per exclusive routed remediation lead; platform risks: failure mode: Municipal portal IP blocking or deceptive official-notice complaints; trigger: Aggressive unthrottled scraping of Accela/EnerGov portals or styling outreach like an official city abatement order; impact: Portal IP block or city attorney cease-and-desist notice; detection metric: Portal HTTP 403/429 rate and zero municipal impersonation complaints; fallback: Use low-frequency scheduled API/bulk exports and clearly identify all outreach as private commercial contractor/remediation assistance; id: property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency; track id: track_1; name: Automated Commercial/Residential Property-Tax Appeal Arbitrage; mechanism: Ingest county tax-assessor valuation rolls upon annual notice release, run an automated valuation model (AVM) flagging parcels assessed above comparable neighbor equity ratios, and file bulk administrative tax protests for 30–50% of the first year's verified tax reduction.; inputs: Annual county tax-assessor preliminary valuation rolls & parcel GIS characteristics; Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine; Bulk administrative ARB (Appraisal Review Board) protest filing & hearing pipeline; workflow: Ingest county assessment rolls the day annual valuation notices drop and compute each parcel's assessed-per-sqft percentile against direct neighborhood peers; Mail personalized pre-filled protest postcards showing the owner's exact estimated over-assessment and a QR code to sign a zero-upfront-cost contingency authorization; Auto-generate uniform comparable-equity evidence packets, file bulk administrative protests before the county bar date, and collect 30–50% of Year-1 tax savings; metrics: Protest-window mail-to-signed-authorization conversion %; Percentage of appealed parcels receiving an assessment reduction (65–85% target); Average net contingency fee per residential ($150–$450) and commercial ($2,000–$15,000) parcel; platform risks: failure mode: State property-tax consultant licensing requirements or missed county protest bar dates; trigger: Representing property owners for a fee without required state registration (e.g., Texas TDLR Property Tax Consultant license) or missing the 30/45-day county filing deadline; impact: Rejected bulk filings, administrative fines, or zero contingency revenue for the tax year; detection metric: 100% licensed tax-agent sign-off in regulated states and T-minus-7-day bulk filing completion; fallback: Partner with licensed local property-tax consultants/attorneys of record in regulated states and automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing; id: earnest_money_gator_escrow_lending; track id: track_1; name: Earnest-Money Deposit ("Gator") Escrow Lending & Joint-Venture Splits; mechanism: Advance $2,500–$25,000 refundable-contingency earnest-money deposits directly to title escrow under documented JV or promissory protections, with security recorded or perfected where legally appropriate. Negotiate a 15%–30% share of an earned assignment fee or a lawful fixed return; refunds depend on contractual deadlines, valid contingency exercise and escrow release terms.; inputs: Assignable purchase agreement with explicit refundable contingencies, notice procedures and deadline calendar; Verified title escrow account and executed JV or promissory documents with legally appropriate recorded or perfected protections; Borrower diligence, assignment economics and state-specific lending, brokerage, securities and usury review; workflow: 1. Verify assignment rights, counterparty identity, refundable contingencies and the enforceability of the proposed JV or lending structure.; 2. Execute repayment and profit-split documents, perfect any lawful security and transmit the deposit directly to verified title escrow.; 3. Track contingency and assignment deadlines, require documented progress and deliver timely cancellation notices when authorized and necessary.; 4. Reconcile the closing or refund statement, recover deposited principal and collect only the contractually earned fee or lawful return.; metrics: Earned assignment-fee share or fixed return per completed deposit advance; Percentage of active deposits with verified unexpired refund rights and complete documentation; Deposit loss rate and median days from advance to cleared repayment; platform risks: failure mode: A supposedly refundable deposit becomes nonrefundable or disputed; trigger: Missed contingency notice deadline, invalid cancellation or unauthorized contract amendment; impact: Deposit forfeiture, delayed recovery and disputes over assignment proceeds; detection metric: Deposits approaching contingency expiry without documented assignment or cancellation instructions; fallback: Freeze additional advances, seek timely authorized cancellation and pursue counsel-reviewed escrow release or contractual remedies; id: transactional_double_close_flash_funding; track id: track_1; name: 24-to-72-Hour Escrow-Locked Transactional ("Flash") Double-Close Funding; mechanism: Fund the A->B acquisition only after the title agent independently verifies cleared, unconditional end-buyer B->C funds in escrow and an enforceable closing waterfall. Target a 1.0%–2.5% earned funding fee per 1–3 day turn; closing delays, fraud and legal restrictions can impair returns or principal.; inputs: Executed A->B and B->C purchase contracts, title commitment and independently verified settlement-agent credentials; Cleared end-buyer escrow funds, written disbursement conditions and a reconciled same-transaction payoff waterfall; Commercial-purpose funding agreement reviewed for applicable licensing, usury and escrow requirements; workflow: 1. Underwrite both contracts, title exceptions, end-buyer closing conditions and the settlement agent's authority and applicable bonding or insurance.; 2. Independently confirm end-buyer cleared funds and irrevocable disbursement instructions using a previously verified title-agent contact channel.; 3. Wire A->B funding only to approved title escrow after all release conditions are satisfied and the closing sequence is documented.; 4. Reconcile B->C settlement, recover principal and earned fees, and release capital for reuse only after cleared repayment is confirmed.; metrics: Earned funding fees as a percentage of funded principal per completed turn; Median and maximum hours from funding disbursement to cleared repayment; Unrecovered principal and delayed-closing exposure as a percentage of outstanding funding; platform risks: failure mode: Fraudulent wire instructions or conditional end-buyer funds leave the A->B advance unrepaid; trigger: Last-minute beneficiary changes, failed independent callbacks or unresolved B->C release conditions; impact: Loss of principal, prolonged escrow disputes and interruption of capital recycling; detection metric: Count of unresolved wire-verification exceptions and funded closings past contractual repayment deadlines; fallback: Stop disbursement, independently reverify settlement instructions and obtain counsel-directed escrow recovery before further funding; id: social_to_search_ping_post_arbitrage; track id: track_2; name: Social-to-Search Ad Feed & Ping-Post Lead Arbitrage; mechanism: Buy $0.05–$0.12 curiosity clicks on Meta, TikTok, NewsBreak, and native ad networks and route them through a 4-question qualification bridge—replacing fragile $1.50 RSOC/AFD search-feed clicks with direct $45–$180 Ping-Post lead auctions.; inputs: Low-CPC social/native ad hooks ($0.05–$0.12 CPC); Fast 4-question conditional qualification quiz + TCPA consent capture; Real-time Ping-Post lead distribution engine (Boberdoo / Leadspedia / Phonexa) + RSOC downsell feed; workflow: Acquire low-cost social and native clicks using compliant consumer-benefit hooks (tax appeals, solar rebates, insurance audits, surplus claims); Pre-qualify zip code, homeowner/business status, and urgency inside a zero-friction 4-step quiz bridge; Auction verified exclusive leads in real time via Ping-Post for $45–$180/lead and monetize non-qualifying traffic via compliant secondary search/affiliate offers; metrics: Effective media cost per qualified lead (CPL) vs. Ping-Post auction payout; Ping-to-Post acceptance rate (%) and sub-500ms auction response time; Net arbitrage margin after ad spend and buyer returns; platform risks: failure mode: Ad-account ban, RSOC/AFD feed termination, or TCPA consent challenge; trigger: Using fake 'government stimulus' ad bait, forcing accidental ad clicks, or selling leads without one-to-one TCPA consent logs; impact: Ad account suspension, feed clawbacks, or buyer lead rejections; detection metric: Ad disapproval rate, buyer return rate >5%, and TrustedForm/Jornaya certificate match rate (100% required); fallback: Enforce 100% factual ad hooks, log cryptographic TrustedForm/Jornaya session certificates on every form submit, and diversify across 5+ direct lead buyers; id: tcpa_litigator_scrub_honeypot_arbitrage; track id: track_2; name: TCPA Serial-Plaintiff Docket Scraping & Real-Time Litigator-Scrub Firewall Tollbooth; mechanism: Offer consent-first outbound compliance screening using lawful docket-derived risk signals alongside mandatory do-not-call and revocation checks; plaintiff matching neither authorizes contact nor replaces TCPA compliance.; inputs: Permitted public docket data with identity confidence scores; Consent provenance, revocations, and suppression lists; Applicable calling rules and customer retention policies; workflow: 1. Ingest permitted docket records with source dates, minimization, and human identity review; 2. Check consent, do-not-call status, revocations, and calling restrictions before optional risk enrichment; 3. Suppress noncompliant contacts and route uncertain matches to review without planting honeypots or provoking claims; 4. Serve auditable screening decisions with correction, deletion, and retention controls; metrics: Contacts blocked for missing consent or suppression match; False-positive identity match rate; Screening latency and stale-record share; platform risks: failure mode: False identity match or false assurance of permission to call; trigger: Stale docket data or treating absence from a plaintiff list as consent; impact: Unlawful outreach, privacy complaints, and customer liability; detection metric: Consent-audit failure rate and upheld identity correction requests; fallback: Disable uncertain enrichment and require independently verified consent and authoritative suppression checks; platform risks: failure mode: The underlying lender accelerates debt after a subject-to transfer; trigger: Enforcement of a due-on-sale clause or a related servicing or insurance default; impact: Immediate payoff demand, refinancing costs, foreclosure exposure and harm to the original borrower; detection metric: Lender acceleration notices, unresolved servicing alerts and reserve shortfall against payoff exposure; fallback: Engage counsel and the servicer, pursue lender-approved assumption or refinancing and use a documented lawful sale or payoff exit if necessary; text.title: Evidence before inference. Assumptions made explicit.

circle.title: label: Revenue Potential; score: 24; max score: 25; rationale: Revenue Potential: 24/25. Acquiring low-rate 2.75%–4.25% mortgages Subject-To and reselling via RMLO-underwritten 8.5%–9.9% wraparound notes generates upfront down-payment spreads and multi-year interest arbitrage without landlord repairs.
